chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Fudalah, from Abu al-Mi'za, from Layth al-Muradi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"We do not know a Hajj for God other than Al-Mut'ah. When we meet our Lord, we will say: 'O our Lord, we acted according to Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet.' And the people will say: 'We acted according to our own opinion.' So God will place us and them wherever He wills."

key_terms.الْمُتْعَة: Al-Mut'ah (a specific type of pilgrimage, often associated with temporary marriage or a distinct ritual form in Shia jurisprudence)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Al-Mut'ah Hajj and other forms of Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) asserts that the only Hajj accepted by God is *Al-Mut'ah*, distinguishing it from other forms practiced by the general community. He highlights a theological divergence where the Ahl al-Bayt strictly adhere to the Quran and Prophetic Sunnah, whereas others rely on their own reasoning (*ra'y*), leading to a divine separation on the Day of Judgment. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *Mut'ah* as a distinct, Quranically grounded ritual rather than merely a variant of the standard Hajj.
